question: What was the impact of the global oil crisis of 1973 on the Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-1979)?

options.text: It had no significant impact on the plan.
Led to a reduction in agricultural focus

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Caused economic disruptions and re-prioritisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **global oil crisis of 1973** was triggered by the **Arab Oil Embargo**, resulting in a sharp increase in crude oil prices worldwide.
 
• The oil crisis had a significant impact on India’s economy, especially during the planning of the **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–1979)**.
 
• This economic shock disrupted the government’s planning process and forced the **re-prioritisation of developmental goals**.
 
• Higher oil prices increased the **import bill**, leading to a rise in inflation and a deterioration in the balance of payments.
 
• The plan had to address the issue of **energy security** and focus on reducing dependence on oil imports by promoting domestic energy production.
 
• The crisis underscored the importance of **resource mobilisation** and necessitated adjustments to the original plan, including curtailing ambitious expenditure.
 
• The government shifted focus to sectors like **agriculture and rural development**, which were deemed critical for ensuring food security and employment in the face of economic instability.
 
• The plan also emphasised **poverty alleviation programs** and social sector investments to mitigate the adverse effects of the crisis on vulnerable sections of the population.
